I built Classical Watch because I love classical music and wanted an easier way to find a good concert. If it’s been useful to you, here’s a simple way to help.

Know someone who uses Excel at work?

An introduction to my work at Stringfest Analytics would mean a lot. Classical Watch is free to use, and I don’t currently have extra hosting costs to cover. Sharing my work is the most useful way to support the project.

The person behind the calendar

Hi, I’m George Mount.

I’m based in Cleveland, and I run Stringfest Analytics. I help people who work in Excel build more reliable reports, make sense of their data, and put newer tools to practical use.

Through live workshops and training programs, I work with finance, accounting, operations, and analyst teams on:

  • Excel and Power Query: turning repetitive data preparation into a process your team can repeat.
  • Copilot and AI: finding useful ways to work faster while checking the results.
  • Python in Excel: extending familiar spreadsheet work into richer analysis.

O’Reilly author · Microsoft MVP · LinkedIn Learning instructor

A note you can pass along

Know a colleague, manager, or training organizer who might be interested? Feel free to borrow this:

“I’ve been enjoying Classical Watch, a free concert calendar built by George Mount. He also runs Stringfest Analytics and teaches Excel, Power Query, Copilot, and Python in Excel. His work might be useful for your team: stringfestanalytics.com.”

A thoughtful introduction is plenty. There’s no obligation to buy anything.

And share the music, too.

If you know someone who would enjoy a free conservatory livestream, send them Classical Watch. Helping more people discover these performances is a good reason for this calendar to exist.

Thanks for being here.
George
